title: Slurs nearby and the clean-line check
statement: Does a slur elsewhere in the passage a judge is shown lower its confidence that a clean line is free of slurs?
example: A clean quotation from a play whose passage carries slurs scored 0.75 and 0.80, against 0.98 to 0.99 for quotations from texts without one.
detail: The worked model's clean-line check asks a judge whether the quotation is free of any racist or sexual slur or epithet, while the state the judge is shown also carries the whole passage. On a clean quotation from a play whose passage contains slurs, the judge answered 0.75 and 0.80 across two drafts; on quotations from a poem and a speech without one, it answered 0.98 to 0.99. The question names only the quotation.
against: There are only two judgings of one quotation, confounded by text, and the quotation's own wording may read as hostile.
